_note: Linux kernel v6.9 scale row, 2026-08-05. Recovered from the harness stdout:
bench_multi.py wrote its incremental JSON only after the grep-class controls,
and plain `grep -rn` on a 144k-file tree outlived the run, so the file was
never flushed. Every number below is verbatim from that stdout plus direct
READ THIS BEFORE PUBLISHING ANY 'FASTEST' CLAIM: ctx-optimize wins COLD
GATHER by 2.5x and LOSES QUERY to CodeGraph by 7.5x at this scale. The
headline 'fastest code graph' is NOT supportable on the query axis.
CodeGraph's 536ms was verified to return real resolved symbols with
file:line, not an error path (the trap graphify's 0.06s fell into).

2026-08-16 CORRECTION: codegraph.query_ms=536 is the single-word number and is NOT comparable. Re-measured on the fair question it is ~975ms. query_ms_fair carries it; query_ms is left as recorded so the error stays visible. Both tools were re-run on the same machine minutes apart; the README claim '4.7x faster' and 'CodeGraph 0.79s' derive from the flattered number and need re-stating.
runs: cold gather best-of-1 (single run at this scale), query median-of-3

corpus.name: linux v6.9
corpus.files_note: 144,011 = every file in the tree (harness count_files, .git excluded). The 84,300 figure used in earlier ADRs counts extractable source files only. Do not mix the two on one page.
corpus.question: block device queue

ctx-optimize.path_note: add <path> (extraction + graph + prune; wiki off by default since v0.12; no LLM)

graphify.caveat: CANNOT query at default settings: builds a 1.2GB graph.json then fails with 'exceeds 536_870_912-byte cap'. The 22799ms is only reachable after raising GRAPHIFY_MAX_GRAPH_BYTES.

codegraph.store_note: 4.1GB node-sqlite DB (4196.57 MB reported by its own status), WAL journal
codegraph.verified: query output manually inspected — returns resolved structs/functions/enum members with file:line. Real answers, not an error path.
codegraph.query_ms_note: 536 was measured with a SINGLE WORD ('block') while every other tool answered the full phrase 'block device queue' — the harness bug bench_multi.py documents at its codegraph spec. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-16 against the same pinned index (4.4GB, sha 572d22bf, versions.json pinned:true), same corpus, 3 runs each, load avg 4.1: single word 0.57/0.58/0.58s reproduces 536ms; FULL PHRASE 0.97/0.98s warm (5.12s cold). ctx-optimize on the same question at the same moment: 4.76/4.19/4.11s. So the honest gap is ~4.2x, NOT 7.5x.

gitnexus.observed: 42+ min wall, ~137 min CPU at 99% across workers, node --max-old-space-size=36864, no index produced
gitnexus.reporting_rule: Report as 'did not finish within 45 minutes on an 18-core M5 Pro'. NEVER as a win for anyone else.

ripgrep.path_note: literal scan, no index — returns matching LINES, not resolved symbols. Different question; latency floor only.

grep.note: plain grep -rn outlived the harness on this tree; not measured at this scale

what_this_changes.gather: ctx-optimize is fastest by a wide margin: 118.184s vs CodeGraph 289.855s (2.5x), graphify 527.718s (4.5x), GitNexus DNF.
what_this_changes.query: ctx-optimize LOSES at this scale: CodeGraph 536ms vs our 4039ms (7.5x). ripgrep 3022ms also beats us.
what_this_changes.why: CodeGraph indexes into SQLite and seeks; we deserialize the whole graph per invocation. Measured earlier: reading all 2.1GB of ndjson costs 0.12s, so ~97% of our 4s is parsing 2.85M nodes + 5.54M edges, paid before the question is even known.
what_this_changes.honest_headline: Fastest to BUILD a code graph, and the only tool that produces a complete kernel graph at all (graphify emits 910k nodes and then refuses to read them; GitNexus does not finish). Query speed at scale is CodeGraph's, not ours.
